outcome: admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The study included 40,309 singleton pregnancies with a live vertex-presenting fetus at or beyond 33 weeks of gestation undergoing a trial of labor and delivery at Kuopio University Hospital between January 2002 and December 2021.
finding: During a 20-year period, a decline in fetal blood sampling was associated with an increase in spontaneous vaginal deliveries and a decrease in nonelective cesarean deliveries, but also coincided with a peak in low 5-min Apgar scores.
mod_finding: The rate of spontaneous vaginal deliveries increased from 83.6% to 87.6%, while nonelective cesarean deliveries decreased from 8.4% to 4.3%.
